title: Make the firstmate explainer page followable by newcomers
summary: The page already has a "Start here" intro and glossary (intro.json, xtask/src/site.rs), but the sections after it still show raw ids (t1, c12), "decided by agent/code" fields and terse state tags that a newcomer can't read. I'll make those sections self-explanatory with cited plain-language lead-ins and card summaries, so a reader who has never seen firstmate can follow the page top to bottom.

defaults_applied.how: The page is written for an outside reader who knows nothing of firstmate.
Every new sentence cites claim ids; the renderer rejects uncited ones.
New renderer behavior gets xtask tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change to the renderer and intro text.
Recovered the page source and existing intro from the repository instead of asking.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience is a reader who has never seen firstmate and opens the published GitHub Pages page; the page is built by `cargo run -p xtask -- site` from studies/firstmate-work-handling.
The deployed page may lag the repo's existing intro; I assume the remaining gap is in the sections after 'Start here', which show ids and jargon unexplained.
Every factual sentence keeps citing claim ids from claims.json; no new claims about firstmate are invented and the study is not re-run.
The deploy workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml) is not changed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`; the rendered page has a short lead-in under each of the States, Counters, Transitions, and Why sections that says in plain words what the section shows and how to read it, and every firstmate-specific term it uses appears in the glossary.

In the rendered Transitions section, each card shows a plain-language one-line summary of what happens before the trigger/guard fields, and 'agent' and 'code' as deciders are explained. A newcomer can read the cards without knowing the ids.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`; all tests pass, including new ones asserting the lead-ins appear, that every new sentence still cites an existing claim, and that an uncited new element is rejected.
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.
CHANGELOG.md records the change, and the explainer design doc matches the new page structure.

out_of_scope: Re-running or extending the firstmate study and adding new claims
Changing the pages workflow or hosting
Visual redesign beyond what readability needs
departures: The request is vague about what is unclear on the page, and an intro already exists, so acceptance risk is slightly higher than the reference.
